label: App Bar
title: App Bar
summary: Keep page identity, navigation and a few relevant actions together at the top of a view.
corePrinciple: Use the bar to orient people. Keep its title short and its actions focused.

anatomy.title: Three slots give the bar its hierarchy
anatomy.description: The leading slot orients people, the centered middle slot identifies the page, and the actions slot keeps only relevant actions in reach.
blocks: Back or a product mark establishes where the page sits in the flow.
The SubPage title stays centered inside the 192px middle slot.
Use a small set of public actions that support the current page.

configuration.title: Choose the page relationship first
configuration.description: MainPage gives a view its identity. SubPage supplies a back relationship and centers its title independently from the side slots.
blocks: The published MainPage story pairs JioDot with low-emphasis add and Avatar actions and leaves the middle slot empty.
The guide supplies a public IconButton with a Go back label so the leading action has a clear accessible name.

states.title: State belongs to the child action
states.description: AppBar owns the arrangement. Its IconButton children own enabled and disabled feedback, so the state communicates what is available on this page.
blocks: Child action references · use the playground above for interaction feedback.
Use the actions slot when the page has a useful next action.
Disable a child IconButton when its action is temporarily unavailable.
Configure the bar type and slots, then configure availability on the public child action that needs it.

sizing.title: The host sets the available width
sizing.description: AppBar derives its height from its public padding and children. On SubPage, the middle content is centered in a 192px box and clips or truncates when a crowded title has nowhere to go.
blocks: Side slots have room while the middle remains centered.
At up to 360px of content width, one focused action leaves room; longer titles or extra actions compete with the side slots.

content.title: Make the title and actions earn their space
content.description: A short title helps people orient quickly. Each action should support the page they are on and remain understandable from its accessible label.
blocks: Use the page name people need to recognize, then move supporting detail into the page body.
Show only the few actions that help someone complete the current task.
Use the public IconButton accessibilityLabel so icon-only controls remain discoverable.

inContext.title: Move between related pages with one contract
inContext.description: The product flow owns navigation state. AppBar presents the current destination and invokes the public child actions supplied by that flow.
specimen: See recent payments and transfers from this page.

doDont.title: Make the relationship easy to scan
doDont.description: Use the page title, action count, and page type to make the next destination and its available actions clear.
blocks: A short title stays readable in the centered middle slot.
Put the page brief inside the bar
The centered slot clips extra words when a title carries the whole page brief.
One low-emphasis action leaves the destination and the next step easy to scan.
Every extra control competes with the few actions that support the current task.
Use SubPage for a child destination
The supplied Go back action makes the relationship to the parent page explicit.
Use MainPage identity for a detail view
JioDot and an empty middle slot describe a top-level destination, not a child page.

sources.title: Grounded in the published component
sources.description: This guide separates designer-configurable slots and page types from package behavior that affects sizing and accessibility.
blocks: MainPage, SubPage, long title, and progress examples

Examples use the public AppBar, IconButton, JioDot, and Avatar exports plus the published Storybook TitleText fixture for the middle slot. The source fixture uses explicit 16px bold text and a color literal keyed to its Light/Dark mode; this is documented provenance rather than a claim that Figma specifies the typography. Figma and package behavior differ on fixed reference heights and MainPage’s JioDot default; the guide also supplies a named public back action because the package default has no accessible name.
